cues.caption: In Fante country, Anansi gathered wisdom into a pot. Offended by his neighbors, he planned to keep it from them.
cues.title: Wisdom in a pot

cues.caption: He carried the pot against his chest and tried to climb a tall tree. The pot kept getting in his way.
cues.title: The difficult climb

cues.caption: His son Kweku Tsin watched below. Why not carry it on your back, the boy suggested. Anansi stopped climbing.
cues.title: Kweku Tsin's advice

cues.caption: If all wisdom was inside his pot, how could his son know better? Anansi dropped the pot, scattering wisdom abroad.
cues.title: No one knows everything

cues.caption: The birds wanted a king. They argued about size, strength, and beauty, before choosing a contest of height.
cues.title: The birds assemble

cues.caption: Vulture climbed toward the sun. Tiny Tink-tinkje rode unnoticed among his feathers, saving the strength of his own wings.
cues.title: Under Vulture's wing

cues.caption: Whenever Vulture claimed the crown, the little bird flew just above him. His small voice declared that he was higher.
cues.title: A voice from above

cues.caption: Angry birds chased the trickster into a hole. Owl guarded it, but fell asleep, and Tink-tinkje slipped away.
cues.title: The sleeping guard

cues.caption: Stories belonged to Nyankupon. Anansi asked to name them after himself. First, he must deliver bees, a great snake, and a tiger.
cues.title: Nyankupon's bargain

cues.caption: Anansi argued aloud that the bees could not fill his jar. They flew inside to prove him wrong, and he sealed it.
cues.title: The jar of bees

cues.caption: He challenged the snake to match a stick, then bound it in place. Another deception helped him lead away the tiger.
cues.title: Measuring the snake

cues.caption: Nyankupon saw that Anansi had fulfilled the bargain. The old stories could now bear the spider's name.
cues.title: A name for the tales

cues.caption: A monkey shared fruit from a coastal fig tree with a shark. Their friendship lasted through many visits.
cues.title: Fruit above the sea

cues.caption: The shark offered a journey home on his back. Halfway there, he admitted his ruler wanted the monkey's heart.
cues.title: An invitation underwater

cues.caption: The monkey said he had left his heart in the tree. Believing him, the shark turned toward the shore.
cues.title: A quick answer

cues.caption: The monkey climbed to safety and refused another journey. He would not mistake a dangerous invitation for friendship again.
cues.title: Safely among the branches

cues.caption: In this recorded Zulu telling, the creator sends Chameleon to tell human beings that they will not die.
cues.title: The first message

cues.caption: Chameleon travels slowly, stopping to feed along the way. The hopeful message has still not reached the people.
cues.title: Along the road

cues.caption: A second messenger, called Salamander in this translation, is sent with a different message: human beings must die.
cues.title: The faster messenger

cues.caption: The faster messenger arrives first. The tale holds mortality and lost possibility within the distance between two journeys.
cues.title: The message that arrived

cues.caption: In the monkey's tale, Hare persuades a washerman's donkey to visit Lion. An attractive promise conceals an ambush.
cues.title: A promise from Hare

cues.caption: Lion's first attack fails, and the donkey escapes. Hare returns with reassurance, asking the donkey to believe him again.
cues.title: The first escape

cues.caption: The donkey returns and does not survive. Later, Hare takes the heart and ears that Lion had reserved for himself.
cues.title: The second visit

cues.caption: Hare argues that a creature with judgment would never have returned. The monkey finishes his warning and rejects the shark.
cues.title: A dangerous excuse

cues.caption: Goso teaches children beneath a calabash tree. A gazelle dislodges a fruit, which falls and kills the teacher.
cues.title: Beneath the calabash tree

cues.caption: His pupils seek someone to punish. They accuse the south wind, then the wall that stops it, then the rat.
cues.title: The search for a cause

cues.caption: Each accused points toward another power: cat, rope, knife, fire, water, ox, and tick. The chain finally returns to gazelle.
cues.title: A circle of explanations

cues.caption: Unable to redirect the accusation, the gazelle is killed. The circular tale leaves the pupils' certainty beside their continuing loss.
cues.title: The cost of certainty

cues.caption: Sultan Majnun tends a rich garden, yet a mysterious bird repeatedly eats the ripe dates before he can taste them.
cues.title: The guarded garden

cues.caption: His older sons fail at keeping watch. The youngest asks for a turn, though his father doubts he will succeed.
cues.title: The youngest volunteer

cues.caption: The young watcher stays awake and seizes the bird's wing. It carries him high above the garden, urging him to let go.
cues.title: Wings above the palm

cues.caption: He refuses to release it. The bird brings him safely down, beginning the bargain that carries the longer story onward.
cues.title: Returning to the ground
